contentHtml:
Want to know the secret to cooking delicious gammon steaks? It's all about choosing the right cooking method that suits your taste and timing. Whether you're a fan of juicy, oven-baked gammon or prefer a quick, pan-fried approach, mastering these techniques will turn you into a gammon steak expert in no time. As we have discussed before how to cook samphire, get ready for this one as well;

In this article, you will learn:

  • How to select and prepare your gammon steaks for cooking.
  • Various methods to cook gammon steaks, ensuring perfect results.
  • Simple and delicious recipes to enhance your gammon steak meals.

Ready to become the master of your kitchen with these gammon steak cooking secrets? Let's get started and make your meal unforgettable!

Preparation Tips

Before you start cooking, it's important to set yourself up for success with some simple preparation tips. Preparing your gammon steaks properly can make a big difference in how they taste.

How to Select the Best Gammon Steaks

  • Look for Freshness: Fresh gammon steaks should have a pinkish-red colour with a firm texture. Avoid any pieces that look dry or have a dull colour.
  • Check the Thickness: For even cooking, choose steaks that are about the same thickness. Around 1 inch thick is ideal for most cooking methods.
  • Consider the Fat: A little bit of fat on the edges can add flavour and help keep the steaks moist during cooking, but too much fat might be overwhelming.

Serving Sizes: How Much to Buy

  • For a Main Dish: Typically, one gammon steak per person is enough. Each steak usually weighs about 200 grams (7 ounces).
  • For a Lighter Meal: If you’re serving other hearty side dishes, you might only need half a steak per person.

Proper Storage Techniques

  • In the Refrigerator: Wrap the steaks tightly in plastic wrap or place them in an airtight container. They will keep for up to three days.
  • In the Freezer: For longer storage, freeze the steaks on the day of purchase. Wrap them individually and use them within three months for the best quality.

Cooking Methods Explained

Now that you know how to pick and prepare your gammon steaks, let’s explore the various methods you can use to cook them. Each method has its benefits, so you can choose based on what you like and what tools you have in your kitchen.

Oven-Baked Gammon Steaks

Why Try It: Baking gammon steaks in the oven is a fuss-free method that allows the flavours to meld beautifully. It’s also great for cooking multiple steaks at once.

How to Do It:

  1. Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
  2. Place the gammon steaks on a baking tray lined with foil. You can add some herbs like rosemary or thyme for extra flavour.
  3. Bake for about 20-25 minutes, turning once halfway through, until they are golden and cooked through.

Pan-Frying Gammon Steaks

Why Try It: Pan-frying is quick and gives the steaks a deliciously crispy exterior.

How to Do It:

  1. Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. You can add a small amount of oil or butter for extra flavour.
  2. Cook the gammon steaks for about 3-4 minutes on each side until they are nicely browned and cooked to your liking.

Grilling and BBQ Techniques

Why Try It: Grilling gives gammon steaks a smoky flavour and appealing grill marks, perfect for outdoor cooking.

How to Do It:

  1. Preheat your grill to medium-high heat.
  2. Brush the gammon steaks with a little oil and season as desired.
  3. Grill for about 3-4 minutes on each side, depending on thickness.

Innovative Methods: Air-Frying and Using a George Foreman Grill

Why Try It: These methods are great for reducing added fats while still achieving a crispy texture.

How to Do It:

  • Air-Frying: Preheat the air fryer to 200°C (390°F). Cook the gammon steaks for about 10 minutes, flipping halfway through.
  • George Foreman Grill: Preheat the grill. Cook the gammon steaks for about 4-5 minutes, or until fully cooked.

Quick Fix: Microwaving Gammon Steaks

Why Try It: When you’re short on time, microwaving can be a surprisingly effective method.

How to Do It:

  1. Place the gammon steaks in a microwave-safe dish.
  2. Cover with a damp paper towel to keep them moist.
  3. Microwave on high for about 3 minutes, flipping halfway through.

Featured Gammon Steak Recipes

Once you've mastered the basic cooking methods, you can experiment with these flavorful recipes to bring your gammon steaks to the next level. Here are some tantalizing options that combine simplicity with taste to make your meal unforgettable.

Classic Pan-Fried Gammon Steaks

Ingredients:

  • Gammon steaks
  • Butter
  • Fresh sage leaves
  • Black pepper

Preparation:

  1. Melt butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
  2. Add the gammon steaks and a few sage leaves for flavour.
  3. Fry until golden on each side, seasoning with black pepper to taste.
  4. Serve hot with a side of mashed potatoes or fresh salad.

Oven-baked gammon with Watercress and Mustard Lentils

Ingredients:

  • Gammon steaks
  • Watercress
  • Cooked lentils
  • Wholegrain mustard
  • Olive oil

Preparation:

  1. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
  2. Place gammon steaks on a baking tray.
  3. Mix cooked lentils with mustard and a bit of olive oil, then spoon around the steaks.
  4. Bake for 20-25 minutes.
  5. Serve with fresh watercress on top.

Sticky Glazed Gammon

Ingredients:

  • Gammon steaks
  • Honey
  • Soy sauce
  • Garlic, minced
  • Ginger, grated

Preparation:

  1. Combine honey, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger in a bowl to make the glaze.
  2. Brush the gammon steaks with the glaze.
  3. Either grill or pan-fry as per the instructions in the cooking methods section and reapply glaze as needed.
  4. Serve with steamed vegetables or rice.

Gammon and Cauliflower Cheese Grills

Ingredients:

  • Gammon steaks
  • Cauliflower cut into florets
  • Cheese sauce

Preparation:

  1. Cook cauliflower until tender.
  2. Grill gammon steaks until nearly done.
  3. Top each steak with cauliflower and pour cheese sauce over the top.
  4. Place under the grill for a few minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.

All-In-One Gammon, Egg & Chips

Ingredients:

  • Gammon steaks
  • Eggs
  • Potatoes for chips

Preparation:

  1. Fry or grill gammon steaks to your liking.
  2. Fry eggs in a pan to your desired doneness.
  3. Serve with homemade or oven-baked chips.

Refreshing Gammon Steaks with Apple & Bulgur Salad

Ingredients:

  • Gammon steaks
  • Apples, sliced
  • Bulgur, cooked
  • Lemon juice
  • Olive oil
  • Fresh herbs (like parsley or mint)

Preparation:

  1. Grill or pan-fry the gammon steaks.
  2. Combine sliced apples, bulgur, lemon juice, olive oil, and herbs to make the salad.
  3. Serve the gammon steaks topped with the fresh salad.

Additional Cooking Tips

To ensure your gammon steaks always turn out perfectly, here are some extra tips that can help you refine your cooking techniques and add a little extra flair to your dishes.

Metric vs. Imperial Measurement Conversions

Cooking can sometimes get confusing with different measurement systems. Here’s a quick guide to help you convert between metric and imperial units so that you can follow any recipe effortlessly:

  • 1 ounce (oz) = 28 grams (g)
  • 1 pound (lb) = 0.45 kilograms (kg)
  • 1 inch (in) = 2.54 centimeters (cm)

Keep a conversion chart handy in your kitchen for easy reference.

Detailed Cooking Instructions for Perfect Results

  • Even Cooking: To ensure your gammon steaks cook evenly, let them come to room temperature for about 20 minutes before cooking. This reduces cooking time and helps the meat cook evenly.
  • Resting the Meat: After cooking, let your gammon steaks rest for a few minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, making it juicier and more flavorful.
  • Flavour Enhancements: Experiment with different marinades and spices before cooking to enhance the flavour of your gammon steaks. Simple ingredients like honey, mustard, or soy sauce can transform your dish.

Conclusion

Congratulations! You’ve just explored a range of ways to select, prepare, cook, and serve gammon steaks, turning this simple ingredient into a standout meal. From understanding the basics of gammon steak selection and storage to mastering various cooking methods and experimenting with delicious recipes, you’re now equipped to impress at the dinner table.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is the best way to cook gammon steak?

The best way to cook gammon steak depends on your taste preferences, but pan-frying and grilling are popular methods. Pan-frying offers a quick, flavorful sear, while grilling provides a smoky flavour.

Can gammon steaks be cooked in an air fryer?

Yes, gammon steaks can be cooked in an air fryer. It’s a healthier option as it requires less oil. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C (390°F) and cook the steaks for about 10 minutes, turning halfway through the cooking time.

Does gammon have to be boiled before roasting?

No, it's not necessary to boil gammon before roasting, but doing so can help render some of the excess salt and fat, resulting in a milder flavour and more tender meat. If you choose to boil your gammon first, simmer it in water for about 30 minutes before roasting.

How do you cook gammon steaks in the oven (UK)?

Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Place the gammon steaks on a lined baking tray, optionally topping them with some seasoning or a glaze. Bake for 20-25 minutes, turning halfway, until they are fully cooked and golden.

How to cook gammon steaks in a pan?

Heat a pan over medium heat and add a little oil or butter. Place the gammon steaks in the pan and cook for about 3-4 minutes on each side, or until they are golden brown and cooked through.
